title: Geozone Erasure Certification & Customer Evidence Export
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Problem: Customers subject to data residency and privacy laws request proof that user data stored in specific geographic zones (geozones) has been deleted and that an auditable, tamper-evident bundle of evidence was exported to them. Current RTBF flows are fragmented across services: deletion jobs run, but there is no signed per-geozone certification, nor a standardized customer-facing evidence export that shows the deletion actions, timestamps, and cross-region replication status.

Goal: Build a certified erasure workflow that produces a signed "geozone erasure certificate" and an evidence export package for customers. The package should prove: which geozones were targeted, what objects/records were deleted, the deletion operation IDs, timestamps, storage tombstone receipts, replication/async-copy statuses, and attestations that downstream caches (KV/caching layer) and backups were purged or scheduled for purge. The certificate and evidence bundle must be cryptographically signed by Redwood's compliance service and available for customer download via the Console and programmatically via the Compliance API.

Scope: Design and productize the end-to-end UX, error states, and acceptance criteria; coordinate with Engineering to define schema for evidence bundles, signing protocol (JWT or CMS), retention of evidence copies for audits, and UI/Console export flow. The feature must respect legal-hold overrides, support per-customer geozone scoping, and produce machine-readable manifests (JSON/CSV) plus a human-readable summary (PDF). This ticket covers product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and initial QA. Engineering tickets will handle runtime deletion orchestration, signer service, and storage of evidence artifacts.

Out-of-scope: Implementing lower-level deletion primitives for all storage layers (these are tracked as ENG dependencies), and long-term archival for legal discovery beyond 90 days (separate legal workflow).
acceptance_criteria: Console: Customer can request a geozone erasure certificate for a completed RTBF job and download a ZIP containing: deletion_manifest.json, deletion_audit.csv, signed_certificate.pdf, and signer_proof.jwt
API: Compliance API exposes an endpoint GET /v1/customers/:id/erasure-exports that returns export metadata and a presigned URL for the artifact within SLA (60s).
Signing: All certificates are signed by Redwood's compliance signer; signature verification steps documented in Confluence and reproducible by customers.
Residency: The manifest indicates the geozone(s) targeted and confirms whether any cross-region replicas existed and their deletion status.

Proofs: Evidence bundle includes per-storage-layer receipts (object deletion receipts, KV cache flush logs, and backup purge job IDs) or explicit reason when proof is unavailable (e.g., external backup vendor).

Legal-hold handling: If a legal hold prevents deletion, the Console displays a clear reason and provides exportable hold metadata; no certificate is issued until the hold is cleared or an override is approved by Legal.

notes: Design direction: single-button 'Generate Erasure Certificate' in Customer > Data Residency with an option to include full evidence bundle or certificate-only summary.
Evidence format: ZIP with root manifest 'deletion_manifest.json' listing resources by type, geozone, operation_id, timestamp, and proof pointers.
Signer: Prefer JWT with RS256 for verification interop; fallback to PKCS7/CMS for customers requiring CMS format.
Retention: Redwood keeps a copy of the exported evidence bundle for 90 days for auditability; retention period configurable per-enterprise contract.
Metrics: track export generation time, signature latency, failure reasons, and percentage of exports requiring manual legal review.
